recentItems.title: How does perimenopause change your brain? | Marija Kundakovic | TEDxFordham University
recentItems.description:
Despite making up roughly half the world’s population, women’s health has been drastically understudied—especially the brain and mental health across reproductive stages. This talk explores the critical hormonal changes of perimenopause, the 4–10 years preceding menopause, and how these shifts increase psychiatric risk, including mood disorders, anxiety, and even suicide.

Marija Kundakovic presents groundbreaking research using postmortem human brains to map ovarian hormone effects on the brain at cellular and molecular levels. By combining biomarkers from blood, hypothalamus, and pituitary tissues, her team developed a model to determine menopausal status postmortem—paving the way for precision medicine and female-specific psychiatric treatments. This talk highlights the urgent need for education, new science, and actionable solutions to improve women’s mental health. 

Marija Kundakovic, PharmD, PhD, is a professor in the Department of Biological Sciences at Fordham University. Her lab focuses on hormonal and environmental factors driving sex differences in depression, anxiety, and substance use disorders. Kundakovic has been at the forefront of psychiatric epigenetics research since early in her career. Her lab discovered sex-specific epigenetic regulation in the female brain as a function of the ovarian cycle, providing a new molecular framework to study the female-specific susceptibility to psychiatric disorders. More recently, Kundakovic’s lab established the postmortem tissue biomarkers to study cellular and molecular changes in the human brain across the menopausal transition. Her research has been published in top-tier scientific journals and she is an elected member of the American College of Neuropsychopharmacology and an executive committee member of the Organization for the Study of Sex Differences. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: “May you no longer afraid of going astray, but eager to wander.” | LIU CHENG-YEN | TEDxTCGS Youth
recentItems.description:
Good news: she is currently still in the state of “wandering,” like most of us are. Her story explores the theme of the inescapable bewilderment of life, tough decisions, and self-doubt—featuring raw and brutally honest thoughts and comments that people dare not confront. 
So, buckle up; it’s time for a thrilling roller-coaster ride into the most intense six years of her life. You will see the peaks and valleys of her journey, how she surmounted the obstacles, and how she eventually broke free from the fear of the unknown.
May you leave with a sense of wanderlust for life—no longer afraid of going astray, but eager to wander. https://www.instagram.com/0ak13y_33?stkn=bWg4MWt1emMwbWNw This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: “Losing direction is also a form of direction.” | HUANG TING-HSIU | TEDxTCGS Youth
recentItems.description:
A college student brimming with curiosity about the world believes that life doesn't require rushing to find answers; even losing direction is a form of direction.
From working part-time while studying during her senior year of high school, to working and staying in Orchid Island, hiking around the island alone, and soon going on exchange to the Czech Republic, every step she has taken wasn't because she already knew the answers, but rather, through repeated attempts, she has gradually moved closer to the person she wants to become.
This time, she will share her experiences, titled "Lost," exploring how choices that once seemed like detours have become the most precious scenery in her life when she looks back. https://www.instagram.com/ts_zzz_1110?stkn=MTMwdXQ2NWR4ZWtheg== This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: "Each choice was actually the best choice at that moment." | PEI-CHUN YU | TEDxTCGS Youth
recentItems.description:
For this little girl, the most terrifying thing about being lost is making choices.
In her 19 years of life, she has made many choices. Some may be incomprehensible to others, and some decisions even she herself couldn't understand.
But looking back at each choice over those 19 years, it becomes clear that "each choice was actually the best choice at that moment." https://www.instagram.com/peijun.yu?stkn=MXdwZHBobnIzNThsbg== This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: “Rewriting your own life's direction” | HUANG JIH-HUANG | TEDxTCGS Youth
recentItems.description:
Do you truly believe that the path you're on now is one you chose yourself?
From magic to philosophy, I've found that the human brain is always eager to find answers to the unknown, and life is no exception. I once firmly believed that as long as I followed the map society provided, I would achieve success; until the day university results were released, the words "not admitted" made me begin to doubt those life answers I had never questioned before. This speech will start from my own journey of confusion, rethinking the meaning of "answers," and inviting you to join me in writing your own life's direction after the familiar map has become invalid. https://www.instagram.com/rahulahuang?stkn=MXgwdTNhbm1jbjQyNg== This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: “Finding direction again from the astray.” | HUANG HSIN-YA | TEDxTCGS Youth
recentItems.description:
She skipped over 300 classes that semester, yet never truly stopped learning.
From experiencing headaches and fevers upon entering the school to gradually finding her way again through the library, online courses, and self-study, she was once accused of faking her studies and even doubted whether she had taken the wrong path.
This time, she wants to share her journey of refusing to attend classes and her struggles with self-study, showing how someone who couldn't step into the classroom rediscovered learning and herself through confusion, anxiety, and countless small attempts https://www.instagram.com/emily_from_taiwan?stkn=MW5vcjRlNGNwd2Qw This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. recentItems.title: “The way to get out of the maze of external perspectives.” | LO CHEN-YUN | TEDxTCGS Youth
recentItems.description:
An unremarkable starting point? A frog in a well?
She comes from Hualien, a place others call a "remote area." She doesn't understand why children from Hualien are always viewed with prejudice. On her journey of confusion and searching for solutions, an encounter, a turn in the road, slowly changes everything.

recentItems.title: This is Dreaming | Tarek Abou El Fetouh, Mahmoud Shiha & Hany Mustafa | TEDxEast Katameya
recentItems.description:
What happens when music, visuals, technology, and storytelling stop existing as separate art forms and become a single shared experience? Created by Tarek Abou El Fetouh in collaboration with Hany Mustafa and Mahmoud Shiha, this immersive live performance dissolves the boundaries between sound, sight, and emotion. Blending live music, visual art, digital technology, and narrative, the performance invites audiences to experience unexpected connections between disciplines, cultures, and human expression. Rather than simply being watched or heard, it is designed to be felt—challenging the audience to rethink how creativity emerges when seemingly different worlds collide. Tarek Abou El Fetouh is a multidisciplinary artist whose work spans music, finance, technology, and immersive storytelling. Inspired by cultures, sounds, and experiences from around the world, he creates performances that blend live music, innovation, and narrative into thought-provoking experiences. His work explores the unexpected connections between disciplines, demonstrating how creativity flourishes at the intersection of seemingly unrelated worlds

Mahmoud Shiha is a music producer, visual artist, and co-founder of EPIC 101 Studios. His work merges sound, visuals, and storytelling to create immersive, multi-sensory experiences that evoke emotion and spark imagination. By blending artistic expression with technology, Mahmoud explores new ways of connecting people through creative worlds where music and visual art become one.

Hany Mustafa is an Egyptian singer, songwriter, and musician celebrated for blending diverse musical traditions into a distinctive sound. Drawing inspiration from Indian and Arabic pop to world music, his work combines rich storytelling with powerful performances that bridge cultures and emotions. As one of the driving forces behind Egypt's evolving underground music scene, Hany continues to push creative boundaries through music that connects people across genres and generations. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: "Learn to find your way out of confusion by asking questions." | WU CHENG-YUN | TEDxTCGS Youth
recentItems.description: At the age of 14, she was diagnosed with a rare disease called Reber's optic neuropathy, which caused her vision to drop from 1.0 to near blindness. recentItems.title: Ce facem cu ce ni s-a făcut? | Bobo Burlăcianu | TEDxCopou
recentItems.description: Bobo Burlăcianu vorbește cu umor și autoironie despre creativitate și despre curajul de a nu lua nici succesul, nici eșecul prea în serios. Din experiența sa artistică, arată cum joaca, improvizația și asumarea propriului fel de a fi pot transforma stângăciile, dezamăgirile și chiar ridicolul în materie primă pentru creație. Un discurs despre autenticitate, libertatea de a greși și puterea umorului de a transforma experiențele amare ale vieții în povești care ne fac să râdem, să ne recunoaștem și, uneori, să vedem lucrurile altfel. Bobo Burlăcianu este cântăreț, compozitor și autor, cunoscut ca membru al trupei Fără Zahăr și pentru colaborările sale artistice cu Ada Milea. Muzica, umorul și autoironia sunt instrumentele prin care transformă observațiile despre oameni, societate și imperfecțiunile vieții în povești care provoacă deopotrivă râsul și reflecția. Stilul său artistic se construiește la întâlnirea dintre sensibilitate, spirit critic și luciditate, într-o permanentă joacă între comic și serios. Prin creațiile sale, Bobo invită publicul să privească realitatea din perspective neașteptate și arată cum umorul și creativitatea ne pot ajuta să înțelegem mai bine lumea și, uneori, pe noi înșine. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: TẠI SAO CHÚNG TA CẦN TIẾP TỤC MẮC SAI LẦM TRONG THỜI ĐẠI AI?  | NGUYEN TRUC ANH | TEDxMoc Chau
recentItems.description:
Artificial intelligence is making learning faster and easier than ever. With a single question, we can receive an answer, generate an essay, or solve a difficult problem within seconds. But could this convenience cause us to lose something essential to the process of growing and learning?

Drawing from her own experience of using ChatGPT for schoolwork, Nguyễn Trúc Anh discovered that making mistakes, struggling, and finding answers independently are still essential parts of learning. When AI can provide solutions almost instantly, it becomes easy to skip the process of trying, failing, thinking, and discovering for ourselves.

This talk does not present AI as the enemy of education. Instead, it asks an important question: How can we use AI as a tool without losing our ability to think for ourselves?

AI can show us the road, but it cannot walk it for us.- AI đang khiến việc học trở nên nhanh chóng và dễ dàng hơn bao giờ hết. Chỉ với một câu hỏi, chúng ta có thể nhận được câu trả lời, một bài viết hay thậm chí là một lời giải hoàn chỉnh. Nhưng liệu sự tiện lợi đó có khiến chúng ta đánh mất một phần quan trọng của quá trình trưởng thành?

Từ trải nghiệm của chính mình khi sử dụng ChatGPT để làm bài tập, Nguyễn Trúc Anh nhận ra rằng việc mắc sai lầm, gặp khó khăn và tự mình tìm kiếm câu trả lời vẫn là những phần không thể thiếu của quá trình học hỏi. Khi AI có thể đưa ra đáp án gần như ngay lập tức, con người rất dễ bỏ qua quá trình thử, sai, suy nghĩ và tự khám phá.

Bài nói không xem AI là kẻ thù của giáo dục, mà đặt ra một câu hỏi quan trọng: Làm thế nào để chúng ta sử dụng AI như một công cụ mà không đánh mất khả năng tự suy nghĩ?

AI có thể chỉ cho chúng ta con đường, nhưng nó không thể bước đi trên con đường đó thay chúng ta. luongthuylanh90@gmail.com This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
